title: Babel-Ashur
imageCaption: Babel-Ashur — full island reference preserved in the archive.
dek: An immense island of jungle, mountain caverns and a dry caldera beneath a floating city. Its surviving people hide the seeds of a lost Tree while the Called struggle to turn shelter into a lasting defense.

facts.Central feature: Dry caldera beneath a floating island and frozen city
facts.Southern subregion: Greyward Littoral · landing, pathways, shelter and cavern approaches
facts.Expedition status: Ryvyt is dead after the guarded return. Four companions escape; retrieval fails. The western mist persists.
facts.People: Scattered native tribes; the community at Skylight Refuge
facts.Seed: One entrusted to Elenia; other seeds and planting knowledge known through survivor testimony

body:
Babel-Ashur is an immense island where a coastal refuge stands between hunted people and the powers occupying their land. Its southern jungles lead to mountain caverns; beyond the ridge lies a dry caldera beneath a floating, frozen city. To the west, green mist turns the search for knowledge into a struggle to keep companions from losing themselves.

The island’s surviving inhabitants have guarded seeds, preserved stories and kept children alive long before the Called learn their names. Their help changes the expedition from a search for an enemy into a defense of a home. The fighting wins shelter and temporary openings, but leaves losses that no victory can quietly erase.

Jungle, mountain and caldera

The coast is thick with life. Narrow canyons offer concealment; mountain paths bring cold, exhaustion and a view into a dry interior. Beyond the ridge, geysers and sandstorms cross a caldera beneath a colossal floating island. On that island stands a frozen city. These landscapes impose different kinds of danger on travelers who first learn to survive a single night near the shore.

A later expedition distinguishes four broad environments: titans in the caldera, magical machines in the caverns, monsters in the jungle and giants in the mountains. That distinction helps explain why knowledge of one route cannot stand for knowledge of the whole island. The Greyward Littoral is the named southern coastal subregion; the Luminar Spires have their own coastal account. Their exact relationship to every inland feature remains incomplete.

Greyward Littoral · the southern foothold

The annotated map of Greyward Littoral begins at Landing Beach. A branching watercourse cuts through the wooded coast, with the Volcanic Crystal Well and Caverns Below toward the northern highlands. Skylight Refuge lies among the western rock formations; Unmarked Ruins and the Sulphuric Swamps occupy the eastern side. Dotted Safe Pathways connect the expedition landscape.

Those names describe a coast people must learn to use. The beach leaves a company exposed, the canyons can keep larger hunters out, and a familiar trail can reduce the risk of being found. The map gives travelers a foothold; its marked safety remains local and conditional. Read the routes and their quest history →

Across the ridge · the island in the sky

The crossing recorded on 27, Month of Talan, Year 3 is physically costly. Eugene fractures an ankle, Elenia injures a foot and Wren struggles with the altitude. They stop to help one another, then press below the clouds. What opens before them is a wasteland rather than another stretch of jungle: a vast dry caldera, active geysers and blowing sand.

Above it floats an island several miles across, carrying a frozen city. Eugene can make out small flying shapes around it, too distant to identify. Elenia sees movements below on a scale that dwarfs giants. The party considers ways to reach the city but favors returning with more help. Seeing the destination has not yet made it accessible.

At the later campfire, Kyrin gives the floating island a name: Ashur. He remembers a beautiful land and pure waters flowing down from its Tree. The ridge establishes the visible caldera and city; Kyrin supplies a survivor’s memory of what the place once meant.

The first foothold · a night under the open sky

Before there is a refuge to defend, Wren has to find a place to sleep. On 30, Month of Hope, Year 2, she leads the company from the exposed coast into narrow canyons. She declines a light that might attract other creatures and rigs a simple alarm. The first cramped, wet stopping place gives way to a wider cavity open to the sky.

Eugene, deeply uncomfortable in the constricted approach, settles beneath the opening and breathes freely again. Arjahn judges the place defensible against creatures unable to climb or fly. Wren and Aravil arrange watches while the others prepare food and bed down. The party earns one safe night. In time, that provisional camp becomes Skylight Refuge, the base to which injured companions and displaced residents will return.

The survival crisis · May 2026

On 5 May 2026, Mya appeared battered amid a crisis severe enough to raise the possibility that nearly everyone else had already left. She insisted that all lands were worth saving and revealed that Babel’s Shard was not simply a tree, though the mechanism by which it protected the island remained unknown.

Arjahn explicitly calls himself part of the Vanguard and says the remaining company feels as though it is losing. The statement establishes his own identification with the front, while a complete roster and command structure remain unrecovered. In the same exchange, Mya said the gods believed there were too few Knights—or that those who remained were too weak—and presented a strategic choice: pass power and knowledge to a next wave, or reunite and prove the gods wrong.

The prisoners in stone

The early cavern expeditions leave Aravil a captive. In the rescue recorded on 6, Month of Physisia, Year 3, Olokun, Elenia and Arjahn first follow a mapped route through unusually tame wildlife and rocky ground. Near Olokun’s weathered painting, a line of pebbles leads to another image concealed by vines. The adventurers recognize a seed-like heart and begin to understand that people have been preserving something their enemies want.

They then leave for Gael and open a Gate into the cavern trophy room. It is crowded with petrified people fixed to the floor. Aravil’s newer fastenings can be broken, and Elenia restores her movement. The others cannot simply be carried away. Arjahn, believing death preferable to continued imprisonment, shatters many statues as approaching footsteps force a retreat. Their fragments injure the rescuers. A final intact statue falls partly through the Gate, and the company drags it to safety before the opening closes.

Aravil is alive; the other rescued person remains stone when Elenia’s dispelling fails. The success and the destruction belong to the same attempt. At the later campfire Arjahn admits what he did, and Kyrin insists on answering questions about his own condition. His presence gives the cavern history a living witness, without supplying the names or fates of every prisoner.

The people who kept the seeds

The recovered expedition account follows a rescue from the caverns into a community at Skylight Refuge. A nomad entrusts Elenia with a golden seed after Mya’s light frees the captives. At a later meal, Kvethe, Quille, Omari and Kyrin speak for themselves about scattered tribes, interrupted succession, lost farms and the daily labor of survival. Rhea is also named among the listeners. Their stories are testimony, not a complete reconstruction of the island’s ancient history.

Kyrin names the floating island Ashur and remembers the waters of its tree. Omari repeats stories learned from elders while explicitly admitting not having seen that island. The accounts include both memory and inherited tradition, without treating them as interchangeable proof.

Read the full story: The Blood Painting · The Captives and the Seed.

Scattered tribes and guarded knowledge

Kvethe explains why rescuers cannot ask one group for a complete roll of the island’s survivors. The tribes have scattered and stopped contacting one another. She says their captors can extract memories: knowing another hiding place would endanger it. The ignorance that frustrates the adventurers is also a deliberate defense.

Knowledge has narrowed in another way. Quille was selected to succeed an elder, but a huge tigerlike creature seized that elder in her sleep. The planting tradition and mental protections were entrusted through elders; the loss interrupts that succession. Other sects may hold knowledge this group cannot supply. Kvethe agrees that the entrusted seed may be hidden away from Babel until needed, while insisting on her own right to remain and defend her birthplace.

The adults do not all make the same appeal. Kyrin asks that children be sent away. Kvethe also accepts safety for children, yet refuses to leave herself. Their positions make evacuation a question of people’s different needs and obligations, rather than a single choice made for an entire island.

The garden remembered in stories

Omari carries a history learned from parents and elders. The stories describe Babel as Physisia’s garden, where fruit trees sprang up in her footsteps and her voice sounded like birdsong. Her companion Nami Iroh spent his days speaking the lives of the people into the Tree, so that their memories would nourish the land through its waters.

Then the gods ceased returning, for reasons Omari says nobody truly knows. Some people blamed their own wrongdoing. Other inherited stories describe an Ice King dropping the island in the sky, shattering the land and Tree, then laughing as dust and winter fell. Omari has never personally seen the floating island. Kyrin’s fragments of remembered farms, vineyards, mountain forts and falling sky sit beside that tradition, with a different kind of authority.

For the survivors, stories also answer an immediate need. Their journeys alternate between caves and jungle; food may be worms or grubs eaten without a fire because smoke could betray them. Gartina’s meal briefly makes room for conversation even while monsters draw closer. She urges them to keep telling the stories and singing the names of those they no longer see. Babel’s history survives through that work as well as through the seed.

The threat closes in · July 2026

By 29 July, Babel-Ashur’s monsters were moving closer and becoming hungrier and more aggressive. An unpetrified warrior, other adventurers, and roughly a dozen natives sheltered in a cave while a surviving seed or Shard remained central to the island’s future. The Knights were involved in a hunt connected to Death. None of this establishes what happened to the Vanguard after May; it shows only that the wider crisis continued to worsen.

August · the Refuge holds, with losses

The hunters’ approach forces a divided defense. Olokun, Elenia and Scribonia draw threats away; Arjahn, Eugene and Nymera remain between the other attackers and the civilians. Eugene finds a fighting position away from the refugees, but the defenders are soon spending their reserves to survive.

Eugene’s Wish destroys two attackers and Arjahn revives Nymera after her first death. The diversion returns badly wounded, followed by two beasts. In the renewed fighting Nymera is reduced to ash; Eugene and Scribonia kill the remaining creatures. The narrator confirms that Skylight Refuge is safe, while warning that not everyone is. The ashes are collected for a later attempt to restore her.

This is the immediate history behind the later turn toward the mountain. Defending a shelter has bought survival without removing the enemy stronghold or ending the work of recovery. Follow the defense through its different witnesses →

Read the full story: The Defense of Skylight Refuge.

The mountain assault

In the account posted on 29 August 2026 (UTC), Scribonia and Eugene sustain two weather systems while Elenia and Arjahn redirect water and cast earthquakes. Rain, melting snow, fissures and avalanches reshape the cavern-bearing mountain; lava leaks near the caves and smoke obscures the result. Arjahn carries Eugene away from the flooding ground. The mountain is visibly altered, but the scene does not establish that Abyss was killed or that all captives and civilians escaped.

At the gathering posted on 26 September (UTC), companions describe having collapsed and flooded the stronghold, then turn toward the western mist and Luminar Spires. The Final War calendar dates these scenes from their recorded postings; it does not assign an ancient date to the memories discussed there.

Read the full story: The Mountain Offensive · Flood and Ash.

Mark of the Wild · the cost of gathering

Reconnaissance and supply gathering continue around the larger expeditions. The Mark of the Wild hunts connect Aravil’s field skills, Aerrow’s scouting, Arjahn’s protection and the company’s crafting and building needs. Victories bring components; failed harvests, retreats and deaths show how fragile that work remains.

The February two-person hunt ends with Aerrow dead after an earlier Revivify. The main quest later records Elenia raising him. June and July gathering serves a shelter now shared with rescued people; early October ends with healing and a visit to the coast. These are distinct outings, not one uninterrupted expedition or a general claim that all wildlife belongs to Death.

Luminar Spires

The Luminar Spires are a monumental coastal region saturated with unstable primal magic. During the reconnaissance recorded on 26 September 2026 (UTC), Elenia’s Daylight spell transformed into a reversed-gravity effect, the formations glowed after the spell ended, and the Spires twinkled like stars at sunset.

The western mist

The same expedition investigated a vast sickly-green mist covering essentially the island’s western portion. Elenia says it entered through a rift and distinguishes it from the Pale Man’s Haze. Gartina observed unidentified figures moving beneath it; Arjahn’s radiant test burned it away only temporarily before it regenerated. Proximity does not establish that the mist and Spires share an origin.

October · the mist turns rescue against itself

The October expedition begins at a safer Skylight Refuge: ordinary wildlife is returning to its surroundings. That local improvement does not make the jungle safe. Wren, Scribonia, Olokun, Arjahn, Nymera and Ryvyt encounter a giant blind salamander near the route toward the Spires and mist. Its breath paralyzes companions and Olokun is badly wounded. Ryvyt’s healing and restoration help keep him alive; Olokun lands the final blow. A second rush through the undergrowth proves to be a passing boar.

At the coast, the green mist has nearly reached the shore. The attempt to investigate becomes a rescue as visions of loved ones draw people away from their tethers and turn companions into apparent monsters. Ryvyt dispels Nymera’s effect before Scribonia’s Wish clears the mist for miles. Abyss appears and withdraws during the clearing, answering the earlier uncertainty about his permanent destruction: the mountain assault did not end his activity.

The company survives, but its members need care, rest and difficult conversations. Scribonia collapses and Nymera carries him toward the refuge under Arjahn’s escort. The recorded gain is knowledge of the mist and some ways to resist it. Its permanent removal, the rift’s condition and the island’s broader recovery remain unestablished.

October · an offer refused after the clearing

A figure beside the crystal pillars is first mistaken for Abyss, then identifies himself as Dumuzi. He invites the exhausted adventurers to join him and uses Oya’s safety as an inducement. Olokun and Ryvyt refuse; Scribonia rejects the bargain while challenging his account of what a better world would require. Arjahn answers that a wounded world should be healed and that no single will should choose for everyone. Nymera quietly insists that an imperfect world still needs protection.

Dumuzi also claims that Aria is not dead and is better than before. That is later testimony, not a witnessed return or a reason to erase Talan’s recorded killing. A vision is received during the encounter, but its contents are not available as reviewed text in this packet. The witnessed responses and continuing refusals do not authorize an invented account of what it showed.

The expedition is placed on 18 October 2026 in the Final War calendar. The source sequence ends on 19 October 2026; the source postings and the expedition’s established day remain distinct.

The warded return and the guarded ruins

The later return proves that a company can cross the mist without the earlier visions when its members have the protections checked for this attempt. The beach is now reached by the fog, while the Spires appear to hold it off. Neither observation establishes an island-wide cure.

Deeper in the western jungle, pressed toward the mountains, the travelers find human ruins with no human residents. A larger entrance is defended by three horrors and an attack that rises from the ground. Abyss calls it his home and attributes the surrounding dread to a prisoner. His claim leaves the prisoner and the mist’s origin unresolved.

The retreat takes four companions back to the Refuge. Ryvyt dies after being left behind, and Scribonia’s later attempt to retrieve him fails. Read the full return and loss →

Holding ground and returning home

Babel’s campaign grows out of repeated journeys home. The first canyon shelter becomes a place for civilians and a seed; that responsibility makes hiding, hunting and fortifying part of the same war. Aravil and Aerrow bring fieldcraft to the supply expeditions. Gartina supplies food and care. Wren helps find the original shelter and later refuses to approach the mist as if survival were assured.

Olokun’s paintings become a means of contact with people he has not yet met. Elenia receives the seed, Scribonia plans attacks and rescues, and Arjahn repeatedly has to choose whom he can still reach. Eugene helps save the Refuge and later needs to be carried out of the flood he helped create. Nymera dies defending the base, returns to the company and later carries Scribonia when he can no longer walk unaided.

The return on 1, Month of the Wyrm, Year 3 exposes the limit of that mutual care. Four travelers reach the Refuge; Ryvyt does not. His death is confirmed, while recovery of his body and a completed return to life remain unestablished. The continuing shelter is therefore both a strategic achievement and a place where the survivors must face whom they could not bring back.

Babel after the guarded return

Skylight Refuge still functions as the company’s shelter and recovery base. Ordinary wildlife has returned to its immediate surroundings, but dangerous creatures remain on the routes beyond. The mountain offensive visibly alters the stronghold’s terrain; Abyss’s subsequent appearances prove that it did not end his activity. The Spires resist the returning fog locally, and protections help a later company cross the old visions. Neither gain clears the western island.

The guarded ruins remain hostile. The fate and identity of the prisoner Abyss describes, the reach of the mist, the state of the other tribes and seeds, and a completed planting remain unanswered. The region’s future still depends on reaching people and places the defenders cannot yet secure.

For the people carrying the campaign, follow the Vanguard’s companion guide. For the sequence from shelter to the latest retreat, follow Babel · The Survival Campaign. The quest histories above tell each turning point in full; the Babel timeline keeps their dated changes together.
